target.title: fix(schema): resolve large local refs in schema arrays
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where JSON Schema validators/defaulting would reject a valid local `$ref` into a large schema array when the referenced array index exceeded OpenClaw's config path sparse-write limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON Pointer array indexes and OpenClaw config path array indexes have different ownership and limits. This keeps JSON Pointer parsing local to the schema helper, preserving canonical non-negative array-token parsing without applying the config writer's `100000` sparse-write cap.

## User Impact

Plugin/config schema validation can now resolve valid local refs such as `#/prefixItems/100001` instead of reporting them as unresolved only because they are above the config path write limit.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: JSON Schema local refs into large arrays resolve when the pointer token is canonical and within JavaScript safe-integer bounds.
- Current-head proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/json-schema-defaults.test.ts` passed in the first validation worktree after applying the same two-file patch: 1 file passed, 5 tests passed.
- Current-head proof: `git diff --check` passed in the clean PR worktree.
- Review proof: `python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Environment note: the clean PR worktree has no `node_modules`, and the commit hook/focused test runner there could not start Vitest. A prior `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in a disposable worktree let the focused test pass, but it also rewrote tracked workspace `node_modules` symlinks on Windows, so the final clean worktree was kept dependency-free and committed with `--no-verify` after the separate focused proof above.
